findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC5 with the tier definition: scope the 'downgrade-to-advisory' parameterization to the three per-tier signals (consensus, author-response, margin) and add a separate AC asserting that removing the vintage gate EXCLUDES the candidate entirely.
evidence: Tiered bar: 'A FIRE candidate is BLOCKING only when all four hold: reproduction consensus, author-response corroboration, abs(decision_margin) ... at or above ... MIN_MARGIN, and the vintage gate.'
Tiered bar: 'Any single signal plus the gate proposes ADVISORY.'
AC: 'Each blocking conjunct, removed one at a time from a fire candidate, downgrades it to `advisory` ... verified by parameterized `pytest` over the recorded tier string.'
findings.finding: AC5 states that removing each of the four blocking conjuncts one at a time downgrades the candidate to `advisory`, but the vintage gate is a precondition of BOTH tiers — the Tiered-bar text defines ADVISORY as 'any single signal plus the gate'. Removing the vintage gate therefore leaves the candidate with no valid tier at all (it is excluded/skipped), not downgraded to advisory, so the AC is unsatisfiable for that conjunct.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (blocking-conjunct parameterized AC) vs Approach 'Tiered bar'
scenarios: The parameterized test iterates all four conjuncts; the vintage-gate case cannot produce tier=='advisory' because advisory also requires the gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the AC: one parameterized case over {consensus, author-response, margin} asserting advisory, plus one asserting a fire candidate that fails the vintage gate produces no candidate row (or a skipped/zero row).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that a vintage-gate failure (like a skip-list skip) is recorded as a zero-candidate-count manifest row with its reason, so AC2's 'carries a zero candidate count' holds.
evidence: Vintage gate: 'a `project.`-prefixed overlay criterion, or a new rubric — FAILS the gate and is skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that does not exist.'
Skip list: 'A criterion ... is skipped and appears in the manifest with a zero candidate count and that reason.'
AC2: 'verified by `pytest` asserting a `project.`-prefixed criterion carries a zero candidate count.'
findings.finding: The 'Vintage gate' paragraph says a criterion whose resolved file has no committed history 'FAILS the gate and is skipped' but never states such a criterion is RECORDED in the manifest; only the separate 'Skip list' paragraph defines the 'appears with a zero candidate count and that reason' convention. AC2 nonetheless asserts a `project.`-prefixed (vintage-failed) criterion 'carries a zero candidate count' — i.e. appears in the manifest. Whether vintage-gate failures are emitted as zero-count rows or omitted entirely is left contradictory between the Approach and the AC.
findings.location: Approach 'Vintage gate' and 'Skip list' vs AC2
scenarios: An executor emits vintage-failed criteria as absent from the manifest (matching 'skipped') and AC2 fails; or emits them as zero-count rows and the Vintage-gate prose reads as if they are omitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Vintage gate paragraph: '...and is recorded in the manifest as a zero-candidate row with reason `no-committed-prompt-history`, per the manifest convention.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Vintage-gate packaged-path resolution: derive the built-in packaged file via the prompt-id→filename map (criterion_prompt_id then prompts._packaged_prompt_files, i.e. plan-review-E4 → plan_review_E4.md), rather than asserting the file is literally src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md.
evidence: Plan: 'a project .rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md override when present, else packaged src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md'
src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:49-62 criterion_prompt_id: built-in id → 'plan-review-<id>' (e.g. E4 → plan-review-E4)
src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:162 _packaged_prompt_files maps stem.replace('_','-') → filename, i.e. packaged id 'plan-review-E4' resolves to file 'plan_review_E4.md'
search 'plan-review-E4' in reviewers/index.json → (no matches); reviewers/ listing shows plan_review_E4.md, not plan-review-E4.md
prompts.py:188 confirms only the OVERRIDE side is keyed by verbatim prompt id: '.rebar/prompts/<prompt_id>.md'
findings.finding: The Vintage-gate premise that a built-in criterion's resolved PACKAGED prompt file is 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md' is false: the prompt id for built-in E4 is 'plan-review-E4' but the committed packaged file is 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E4.md' (underscore prefix + underscores). The packaged prompt-id→filename map applies stem.replace('_','-'), so <prompt-id>.md is never the packaged filename for a built-in.
scenarios: The selector forms src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan-review-E4.md, git-logs it, finds no history, and skips E4 as 'no committed history' (AC-2 behavior) — skipping every built-in criterion, the selector's entire target population
findings.suggested_fix: State that the resolved packaged file is looked up through the prompt machinery (get_prompt / reviewers index) — prompt id plan-review-<id> resolving to the underscore-named reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md — and only the .rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md override is named verbatim by prompt id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the vintage gate's prompt-file resolution to the real packaged path `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md` (underscore-prefixed) and the override path `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md`, and reconcile the two naming conventions (raw id vs `criterion_prompt_id`) so the git-log targets a file that exists.
evidence: Plan: 'else packaged `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md`'
src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:49 `criterion_prompt_id` maps `F1` -> `plan-review-F1` (dashed), `project.foo` -> `plan-review-project-foo`
Actual packaged reviewer files are UNDERSCORE-prefixed: `plan_review_G6.md`, `plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_verifier.md` (directory listing of src/rebar/llm/reviewers/)
The dashed prompt id and the underscore packaged filename disagree; a git-log against the plan's template path hits a nonexistent file
findings.finding: The vintage gate's packaged prompt-file path template 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md' does not resolve to any real file, so the git-log lookup finds no history and the gate silently skips every built-in criterion.
scenarios: Real-corpus integration run: git-log against a nonexistent 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan-review-G6.md' returns no commits, so the gate treats every built-in criterion as having no committed history and skips it, emitting an empty/near-empty manifest.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the file via the same `criterion_prompt_id` / `get_prompt` machinery the registry uses (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:352-369) rather than hand-building a path, then git-log whichever concrete file `get_prompt` selected (`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md` override or the packaged `plan_review_<id>.md`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the skip condition as 'the resolved prompt file has no committed git history' (the actual test) rather than equating it with the `project.` prefix, and pick an AC fixture that genuinely lacks committed history (e.g. an uncommitted/new project rubric), since committed project overrides DO have history.
evidence: Plan: 'a `project.`-prefixed overlay criterion ... FAILS the gate and is skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that does not exist.'
.gitignore allowlists committed project prompts: `!.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` (lines 38-41)
tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py:6 references `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` as the committed Pass-1 rubric
A committed override file HAS a git history, so the 'no committed history' premise is false for committed project criteria
findings.finding: The plan asserts a `project.`-prefixed criterion has no committed prompt history and therefore fails the vintage gate, but committed project criteria have their rubric at `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`, which does carry git history — so it would NOT be skipped, contradicting AC#2.
findings.location: Approach → Vintage gate; Acceptance Criteria bullet 2
scenarios: A repo with a committed project.portability rubric: the file has commit history, reviews postdating it pass the gate, and the criterion is NOT skipped — so AC#2's 'project.-prefixed criterion carries a zero candidate count' assertion fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the 'a project.-prefixed overlay criterion' clause from the skip rationale; skip solely on 'resolved file absent from git history', and change AC#2 to use a project criterion whose `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md` is uncommitted.

findings.checklist_item: Restate the project.-criterion skip in terms of the actual git-history query on the resolved file (no origin/main commit touches it), not 'the file does not exist', and reconcile AC2 with that condition.
evidence: Plan: 'A criterion whose resolved file has no committed history — a project.-prefixed overlay criterion, or a new rubric — FAILS the gate and is skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that does not exist.'

criterion_prompt_id maps 'project.<name>' -> 'plan-review-project-<name>' (ids.py:52), a real filesystem-safe prompt id resolvable via .rebar/prompts/plan_review_project_<name>.md (prompts.py:169 resolution order) — such an override lives in the consumer repo and can be committed.
The actual skip trigger is 'git returns no origin/main commit for the resolved path', not 'the file does not exist'; the plan equates the two.
findings.finding: The claim that a project.-prefixed criterion FAILS the gate because 'its resolved file has no committed history' is contradicted by the resolution rule: project.<name> resolves to a real prompt file (plan_review_project_<name>.md) that can have committed history, so AC2's zero-candidate outcome rests on an unstated, possibly-false assumption.
findings.location: Approach > Vintage gate; Acceptance Criteria (project.-prefixed zero candidate count)
scenarios: A project overlay criterion whose rubric IS committed to the consumer repo passes the gate, so AC2 (project.-prefixed carries a zero candidate count) fails.

findings.checklist_item: Specify the gate outcome when a resolved (present) prompt file returns no origin/main commit in the run repo — treat-as-no-history-skip vs. an explicit error — distinct from the file-absent case.
evidence: Gate rule: 'eligible only when review_event_ts postdates the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file'.
Packaged reviewer files ship under site-packages; a consumer/CI repo's origin/main need not track src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*, so 'git log -- <path>' can return empty for a real built-in criterion.
Plan enumerates only the project./new-rubric no-history case (=> skip) and gives no rule for 'file present but no origin/main commit'.
findings.finding: No fallback is specified for the gate's failed sub-step when a built-in criterion's rubric file EXISTS (packaged) but has no origin/main history queryable in the run repo — the exact condition of the committed-corpus integration test.
findings.location: Approach > Vintage gate; Testing (real-corpus integration test)
scenarios: Integration run in a checkout where the packaged rubric path has no origin/main history: every built-in criterion is skipped (empty manifest) or, undefined, the gate throws — either way DoD 'manifest covering every uncovered criterion' is unmet.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve each criterion's prompt file through the existing prompt machinery (e.g. rebar.llm.prompting.prompts, `_prompt_file`/`resolve_prompt`/`prompt_ref_exists`) rather than re-specifying the `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md`-else-packaged path resolution by hand, then git-log the resolved path.
evidence: Plan quote: 'a project `.rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md` override when present, else packaged `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md`'
src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:356 `_prompt_file` resolves 'a user .rebar/prompts/ override wins over the packaged reviewers/ copy'
prompts.py:169/358/440/561 document the same resolution order; prompts.py:489 `prompt_ref_exists` already answers 'does this prompt id resolve (catalog / packaged / .rebar/prompts override)'
registry.py:243-245 names the 'da27 prompt machinery (get_prompt -> ... .rebar/prompts/<id>.md project override)' as the canonical resolver
findings.finding: The Vintage-gate re-specifies prompt-file resolution by hand ('a project .rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md override when present, else packaged src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md') instead of reusing the existing prompt resolver, which already implements this exact override-else-packaged resolution.
scenarios: The plan's hand-rolled resolution drifts from the shared resolver if the override directory convention, variant handling, or packaged lookup changes.
A project criterion whose prompt resolves through the catalog or a non-obvious path is mis-resolved because the bespoke code only knows the two literal paths.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the vintage gate obtains the resolved prompt path via the shared prompt resolver (rebar.llm.prompting.prompts) and only adds the new git-log-of-last-touching-commit step on top of it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the vintage gate resolves the prompt-file's last-touched commit when `origin/main` is absent or shallow (e.g. fall back to a configured base ref / `HEAD` history, or fail loudly), so the selector does not silently drop all candidates on such checkouts.
evidence: Plan quote: 'A review is eligible for criterion C only when review_event_ts (corpus.py:273) postdates the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file'
Plan quote: 'A criterion whose resolved file has no committed history ... FAILS the gate and is skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that does not exist.'

A shallow CI clone (git clone --depth=1, common on GitHub Actions/GitLab CI) has no full commit history for the prompt file, and a checkout without a remote named `origin` has no `origin/main` ref at all.
findings.finding: The vintage gate resolves eligibility against 'the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file', assuming a reachable `origin/main` ref with full history — an assumption that fails in supported venues where `origin/main` is absent or truncated.
findings.location: Approach -> Vintage gate: 'eligible for criterion C only when review_event_ts ... postdates the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file'
scenarios: Platform/venue = CI under a provider using a shallow clone: `git log origin/main -- <prompt>` returns no commit, so every criterion's vintage gate finds no prior commit and every candidate is filtered out — the run produces a degenerate/empty manifest with no error, silently failing the 'covers every uncovered criterion' Definition of Done.

Project location = a checkout with no `origin` remote (workstation clone from a different remote name, or a workspace outside the checkout): the `origin/main` ref does not resolve, so the gate query errors or returns empty and no candidates are selected.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the base ref explicitly (configurable, defaulting to the merge-base or a named branch) and require full history for the resolved prompt files, erroring visibly rather than silently skipping when the required commit history is unavailable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive or validate MIN_MARGIN=0.15 against the corpus's observed decision_margin distribution for flipped-vs-stable pairs (or add a probe/measurement step recording why 0.15 is the flip-safe cutoff).
evidence: '`abs(decision_margin)` ... at or above the constant `MIN_MARGIN = 0.15`'
'The margin constant drops findings close enough to `block_threshold` that a small perturbation flips them — the population that makes a fixture flaky.'
Context cites '551 consecutive review pairs ... flipped verdict 208 times' but does not tie 0.15 to that distribution.
findings.finding: MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 is asserted, not derived. The plan cites concrete reviewer-noise data (208 verdict flips over 551 byte-identical pairs) as the motivation for a margin cutoff, but 0.15 is not connected to that data and no measurement/fixture validates that 0.15 actually excludes the perturbation-flippable population it claims to. It is also declared as a fixed 'constant' though the plan expects its rules to be tuned.
scenarios: 0.15 turns out to admit findings that still flip under reviewer noise, or to over-exclude, and no test would catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a measurement step computing the decision_margin distribution over the equal-fingerprint flip population and pick MIN_MARGIN as the margin above which no observed flip occurs; cite that value rather than asserting 0.15.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the labeled-candidate-manifest schema (fields, tier/direction enums, rank ordering, zero-count/reason rows) in an ADR or design-doc note the sibling emitter can reference.
evidence: 'writes a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST — one JSON document listing, per criterion, each candidate with its direction, its tier, the signals that support it and its rank.'
Non-goals: 'Writing any `.eval.yaml`; the sibling emitter owns spec serialization and its schema.'
No ADR/design-doc for the manifest contract is mentioned in Scope, Testing, or DoD.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new cross-module contract — the 'labeled candidate manifest' consumed by the sibling emitter (named in Non-goals) — but the manifest's schema/field contract is not captured in any ADR/doc/AGENTS.md, and the emitter is explicitly a separate ticket that must read it. The coupling is acknowledged but not mitigated with a documented interface.
findings.location: Approach 'Approach' (manifest description) + Non-goals ('the sibling emitter owns spec serialization')
scenarios: The sibling emitter is built against an undocumented manifest shape and drifts from what the selector emits.

findings.checklist_item: State the criterion-id -> resolved-prompt-file mapping explicitly (built-in <id> -> src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md; project.<name> -> plan_review_project_<name>.md, via criterion_prompt_id), replacing the undefined '<prompt-id>' token.
evidence: Plan: 'a project .rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md override when present, else packaged src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md'
No file 'T8.md' exists under src/rebar/llm/reviewers/; the real file is 'plan_review_T8.md' (directory listing).

criterion_prompt_id (src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:49-62) maps a criterion id to prompt id 'plan-review-<id>' (built-in) or 'plan-review-project-<name>' (project.<name>); registry.py:365-369 shows this exact decoupling ('A built-in id maps to plan-review-<id>').
The gate is load-bearing: it decides review eligibility per criterion, so an unresolved criterion->file rule blocks the whole selection.
findings.finding: The vintage gate resolves a criterion to 'packaged src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md', but the token <prompt-id> is never defined and the bare template does not name a real file — the criterion-id -> prompt-file mapping the gate depends on is referenced but not specified.
scenarios: Executor implements the gate, greps git history for 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/T8.md', finds nothing, and wrongly skips every built-in criterion.
Integration test over the real corpus (AC 'covering every uncovered criterion') resolves zero files and emits an empty/near-empty manifest.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each criterion's prompt file through rebar.llm.criteria.ids.criterion_prompt_id(criterion, gate_key='plan_review'): a built-in id -> packaged src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md (or the .rebar/prompts/plan_review_<id>.md override when present); a project.<name> id -> plan_review_project_<name>.md.
